title: Semiconductors and Electronics: From Doped Silicon to Logic Gates

questions.question: Doping pure silicon with phosphorus (group 15, five valence electrons) produces:
options: p-type silicon with holes as majority carriers
n-type silicon with free electrons as majority carriers
questions.rationale: Four of phosphorus's five valence electrons bond with silicon neighbours; the fifth is freed to roam, making the crystal n-type with electrons as majority carriers.

questions.question: A diode conducts easily when:
options: Its p-side is made negative and n-side positive
Its p-side is made positive and n-side negative (forward bias)
Both sides are at the same potential
It is reverse biased beyond breakdown
questions.rationale: Forward bias (p to +, n to −) shrinks the depletion region and lets current flow; reverse bias widens it and blocks current.

questions.question: Which component converts AC mains electricity into (pulsating) DC inside a charger?
questions.rationale: Diodes' one-way conduction rectifies AC: a bridge of four diodes steers both half-cycles the same direction, and a capacitor then smooths the result.

questions.question: The colour of light emitted by an LED is set chiefly by:
questions.rationale: In an LED, electrons fall across the band gap into holes, emitting photons with energy E = hf — the gap size fixes the wavelength and hence the colour.

questions.question: A solar cell works by:
options: Light-generated charge separation across a p–n junction driving current
Using heat to boil a fluid
questions.rationale: Photons knock electrons loose in the junction; the built-in field sweeps them across, producing a photocurrent — the photovoltaic effect.

questions.question: In a MOSFET, the terminal that controls current flow between source and drain is the:
questions.rationale: The gate voltage opens or closes the conducting channel between source and drain; 'emitter' and 'base' belong to BJTs.

questions.question: An XOR gate outputs 1 when:
questions.rationale: XOR (exclusive OR) is 1 exactly when the inputs are different — 0⊕0 and 1⊕1 both give 0, while 0⊕1 and 1⊕0 give 1.

questions.question: Which gate is functionally complete — capable of building every other gate and hence any computer?
questions.rationale: NAND alone can construct NOT, AND, and OR, so any Boolean circuit — including entire processors — can be built purely from NAND gates.

questions.question: Wiring an XOR gate and an AND gate across the same two inputs produces:
options: A half adder (XOR = sum, AND = carry)
questions.rationale: The XOR output gives the sum bit and the AND output gives the carry bit — the half adder, the one-bit building block of binary arithmetic.

questions.question: Unlike metals, a semiconductor's conductivity:
questions.rationale: Heating excites more electrons across the small band gap, adding carriers — so semiconductors conduct better when warm, the opposite of metals.
